reader_question: How does median household income vary from county to county?
grade_line: Documented: a Census Bureau survey, five years of responses pooled, with its published margins of error
title: Median household income was $80,000 or more in 585 counties and under $50,000 in 371 over 2020 to 2024, when the nation’s was $80,734.
measure_line: Median household income by county, in 2024 dollars, from five years of survey responses, 2020 to 2024, 50 states and DC, in four classes, with the nation above the map.
notes: More than half the counties, 1,707 of 3,143, sit close enough to a class line that their margin of error could put them in the next class, and 182 two classes away, so the map shows a broad pattern and ranks no county.
The Census Bureau publishes no estimate for De Baca County, New Mexico, which is left unshaded. Connecticut’s counties are its nine planning regions.
Alaska and Hawaii are drawn apart and not to scale. The download lists every county with its margin of error.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, Table B19013, median household income, 2020 to 2024, every county in the 50 states and DC, and the United States; Cartographic Boundary Files, 2024, counties, 1:20,000,000. Retrieved November 12 and 13, 2026. Survey estimates in 2024 dollars; margins are wide in small counties.
alt: A map of every county shaded in four classes by median household income. The top class, $80,000 or more, holds 585 counties, many around large cities and on the coasts; the lowest, under $50,000, holds 371, many in the rural South. The nation’s median was $80,734.

notes_internal: Ruling (c) and DL-E1 (D3-1090): breaks at $50,000, $65,000 and $80,000; classes 371, 1,138, 1,049 and 585; 1,707 intervals cross a break and 182 two; De Baca County has no estimate; the nation $80,734 (±$166) from the research lead's national row (RL-1, signed off). The drawing reads the class from census-acs5-county-median-household-income-classes (cartographer_round3_derive.py); the table groups by state and the CSV lists every county (check S81 in cartographer_round3_derive.py --figures).

Ruling (b): sequential steps 1, 3, 4 and 5; no county lines; state lines in the context ink at 0.5 px; the land's edge in the context ink; De Baca in the land ink with the context edge, named in a note.
Ruling (a): no named mark, and no county named in words.

DL-E1's conditions (data lead, signed off): the grouped table prints state, counties, the lowest and highest county estimate as values with no county named, and the count in each class; the CSV carries every county's value, margin and class. The nation's row is not among the drawn rows, since the island reads the counties' geoids back from geo.js in the layer's order; it prints beside the map and in the source file (request D-2).
